name: ap-sql-assistant
description: AP-SQL Assistant — Version 10.6. The core objective of this upgrade is to significantly improve 'Describe What You Need' into an intelligent, schema-aware SQL query assistant capable of generating both simple and complex SQL from natural language WITHOUT requiring manual selection of tables, columns, filters, aliases, decode options, Advanced Options, or joins. A new 'Section 2' reasoning pipeline was added to nl-query-engine.js (interpretRequirement / interpretCrRequirement) — fully additive, leaving every V10.1–V10.5 function byte-for-byte unchanged — that performs: Natural Language Understanding -> Schema Analysis -> Table Identification (name/alias/description/module/token-overlap/distinctive-column-alias discovery) -> Column Identification (name/alias/description fuzzy scoring) -> Relationship/JOIN Identification (automatic multi-hop bridge-table discovery via a FK-adjacency graph, so junction tables the user never mentions are still included automatically) -> Filter Identification (operators, boolean-flag phrasing like 'login is allowed'/'active users', exclusions like 'exclude Basware users', membership filters like 'belong to the Finance group', date ranges like 'between January and March 2026', and thousands-separator-safe numeric parsing) -> Aggregation/GROUP BY/HAVING detection (COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX) -> Decode-request detection ('show X as its description') -> SQL Construction (schema-validated, dialect-aware, read-only) -> Confidence reporting and ambiguity detection (the engine explicitly refuses to guess when multiple schema columns could plausibly satisfy the same vague term, surfacing a clarification UI instead) -> a plain-language 'Explain This Query' panel. sql-engine.js gained backward-compatible aggregate-column support (COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX, with optional DISTINCT), and validation-engine.js was updated to tolerate the '*' wildcard target for COUNT(*). The embedded sample schema gained ADM_USER_GROUP/ADM_USER_GROUP_MEMBER (a many-to-many junction), plus LOGIN_ACCOUNT/LOGIN_ALLOWED on ADM_USER_DATA, SUPPLIER_EMAIL on IA_SUPPLIER, and CREATED_DATE on IA_INVOICE, to support the specification's own worked examples end-to-end. The existing structured Query Builder, Query Builder for CR, Decode functionality, SQL dialect selection, schema management, and all security controls remain completely unchanged and fully available for users who prefer precise manual control — the two approaches (natural language and manual) can be freely combined (Hybrid Mode).
